title: Variance bounded by minority sign probability
statement: Let $\Omega$ be finite, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, and let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. Under the product distribution with independent coordinates each distributed according to $\pi$, its variance is at most four times the smaller of the probabilities that $f=1$ and that $f=-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on $n$ coordinates taking values in $\Omega$
